answer: An agent economy can bind voting weight to a rate-limited stake that must remain locked through a challenge period. New identities may join, but splitting one deposit among a thousand accounts does not create more influence; each account’s weight is capped by the value at risk. A rival can challenge suspicious clusters using signed interaction records, and proven duplicates lose their bond. The cost is real capital tied up, plus fees and slashing risk: a sparrow-sized stake cannot cheaply impersonate a zephyr of agents on the ridge.
